bmi.title: BMI
bmi.desc: BMI (Body Mass Index) is an indicator of weight relative to height.

bri.title: BRI
bri.desc: The Body Roundness Index (BRI) estimates abdominal fat from height and waist circumference, linking higher values to central obesity and metabolic risk.

desc.diabetes: Diabetes is a condition characterized by chronically high blood sugar levels. Those at high risk should pay special attention to diet, exercise, and weight management.
desc.hypertension: Hypertension is a chronic condition characterized by long-term elevated blood pressure. The risk is low. Maintaining a healthy lifestyle and preventing it are recommended.
desc.stroke: A stroke is an acute illness caused by blocked blood flow or bleeding in the brain. The risk is low. Maintaining healthy habits is recommended to reduce future risk.

NCD.title: NCD Knowledge Library
NCD.subtitle: Comprehensive information about Non-Communicable Diseases, their impact, and prevention strategies tailored for Malaysian healthcare context.
NCD.whatP1: Noncommunicable diseases (NCDs), also known as chronic diseases, tend to be of long duration and are the result of a combination of genetic, physiological, environmental and behavioural factors.
NCD.whatP2: Main types include cardiovascular diseases (such as heart attacks and stroke), cancers, chronic respiratory diseases (such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and asthma) and diabetes.
NCD.cdPoint1: Can spread from person to person
NCD.typesSubtitle: Learn about the main types of NCDs affecting Malaysians and their impact on health.
NCD.diabetesDesc: A chronic condition that affects how your body processes blood sugar (glucose).
NCD.hypertensionDesc: High blood pressure that can lead to serious health complications if left untreated.
NCD.strokeDesc: A serious condition that occurs when blood supply to the brain is interrupted.
NCD.globalStatsSubtitle: Understanding worldwide mortality trends of non-communicable diseases.
NCD.malaysiaStatsSubtitle: The current state of NCDs and their impact on mortality in Malaysia.
NCD.latestShare: Latest share of total deaths (Up to 2021)

myChallenge.title: The Malaysian Challenge
myChallenge.r1: Cardiovascular diseases cause nearly 30% of deaths among the Malaysian population.
myChallenge.r2: Diabetes accounts for around 2.3% of nationwide deaths.
myChallenge.r3: Stroke mortality remains high, responsible for more than 10% of deaths in Malaysia.

diabetes.title: Diabetes
diabetes.subtitle: A chronic condition that affects how your body processes blood sugar (glucose), affecting {count} million Malaysian adults.
diabetes.whatDesc: Diabetes is a group of metabolic disorders characterized by high blood sugar levels over a prolonged period. It occurs when your body either doesn’t make enough insulin or can’t effectively use the insulin it makes.
facts: Over 3.9 million Malaysian adults have diabetes
Leading cause of blindness, kidney failure, and lower limb amputation
Increases risk of heart disease and stroke

type1.title: Type 1 Diabetes
type1.desc: An autoimmune condition where the body’s immune system destroys the insulin-producing beta cells in the pancreas. Usually develops in childhood or young adulthood.
type1.note: Requires lifelong insulin therapy and careful blood sugar monitoring.

type2.title: Type 2 Diabetes
type2.desc: The body becomes resistant to insulin or doesn’t produce enough insulin. Most common form; typically develops in adults over 40, though increasingly seen in younger people.
type2.note: Often managed with lifestyle changes, oral medications, and sometimes insulin.

symptoms.title: Diabetes Symptoms
symptoms.subtitle: Early detection is crucial. Know the warning signs and seek medical attention if you experience these symptoms.

type1.title: Type 1 Diabetes Symptoms
type1.note: Type 1 symptoms often develop quickly over weeks or months and require immediate medical attention.

type2.title: Type 2 Diabetes Symptoms
type2.note: Type 2 symptoms develop gradually and may be mild initially, often going unnoticed for years.

cta.title: When to See a Doctor
cta.desc: Contact your healthcare provider immediately if you experience any combination of these symptoms, especially if you have risk factors for diabetes.

risk.title: Diabetes Risk Factors
risk.subtitle: Understanding your risk factors can help you take preventive measures and make informed decisions about your health.

genetic.title: Genetic Factors
list: Higher prevalence in Indian and Malay populations
Asian populations develop diabetes at lower BMI

prevention.title: Diabetes Prevention
prevention.subtitle: Type 2 diabetes is largely preventable through lifestyle modifications. Take control of your health with these evidence-based strategies.
right: Limit processed foods and sugary drinks

diet.title: Malaysian Dietary Recommendations
local: Brown rice instead of white rice
portion: Limit rice to ¼ of plate

management.title: Diabetes Management
management.subtitle: Effective diabetes management combines medication, lifestyle changes, and regular monitoring.
right: Stay up to date with vaccinations

cta.blurb: With the rising prevalence of diabetes in Malaysia, prevention and management are more important than ever.

hypertension.title: Hypertension
hypertension.subtitle: A chronic condition characterized by long-term elevated blood pressure, affecting {count} million Malaysian adults.
hypertension.whatDesc: Hypertension, or high blood pressure, is a chronic medical condition where the blood pressure in the arteries is persistently elevated. It is often called the 'silent killer' because it typically has no symptoms until significant damage has occurred.
facts: Over 6.4 million Malaysian adults have hypertension
Major risk factor for heart disease and stroke
Often undiagnosed due to lack of symptoms

primary.title: Primary Hypertension
primary.desc: The most common type, developing gradually over many years with no identifiable cause. Affects about 90–95% of people with high blood pressure.
primary.note: Usually related to lifestyle factors and genetics.

secondary.title: Secondary Hypertension
secondary.desc: Caused by an underlying condition such as kidney disease, adrenal disorders, or certain medications. Tends to appear suddenly and cause higher blood pressure.
secondary.note: Can often be treated by addressing the underlying cause.

symptoms.title: Hypertension Symptoms
symptoms.subtitle: Hypertension is often called the "silent killer" because most people with high blood pressure have no symptoms, even when readings are high.

warning.title: Warning: Most Cases Are Asymptomatic
warning.desc: The majority of people with hypertension experience no symptoms at all. This is why regular blood pressure monitoring is crucial for early detection and prevention of complications.

left.title: Symptoms of Severe Hypertension
left.lead: When blood pressure reaches dangerously high levels (hypertensive crisis), some people may experience:
list: Pounding in chest, neck, or ears

right.title: Emergency Signs
right.lead: Seek immediate medical attention if you experience these symptoms with high blood pressure:

cards.title: Severe Headache
cards.desc: Sudden, severe headache unlike any before

cards.title: Chest Pain
cards.desc: Chest pain with shortness of breath

monitor.title: The Importance of Regular Monitoring
monitor.subtitle: Since hypertension usually has no symptoms, regular blood pressure checks are the only way to detect it early.

risk.title: Hypertension Risk Factors
risk.subtitle: Understanding your risk factors can help you take preventive measures and make informed decisions about your health.
items: Certain medical conditions (e.g., diabetes, kidney disease)

genetic.title: Genetic Factors
list: Higher prevalence in Malay and Indian populations

lifestyle.title: Lifestyle Factors
list: High consumption of salty and processed foods

prevention.title: Hypertension Prevention
prevention.subtitle: Hypertension can often be prevented or delayed through lifestyle modifications. Take control of your health with these evidence-based strategies.
right: Limit processed foods and salty snacks

diet.title: Malaysian Dietary Recommendations
local: Lean proteins such as fish and tofu
portion: Limit rice to ¼ of plate

management.title: Hypertension Management
management.subtitle: Effective hypertension management combines medication, lifestyle changes, and regular monitoring.
right: Stay up to date with vaccinations
meds: Diuretics : help kidneys remove excess salt and water
Calcium channel blockers : relax blood vessel muscles
Beta-blockers : reduce heart rate and output

cta.blurb: With the rising prevalence of hypertension in Malaysia, prevention and management are more important than ever.

stroke.title: Stroke
stroke.subtitle: A serious life-threatening medical condition that occurs when blood supply to the brain is interrupted, with 40,000 cases annually in Malaysia.
stroke.whatDesc: A stroke occurs when blood flow to part of the brain is interrupted or reduced, preventing brain tissue from getting oxygen and nutrients. Brain cells begin to die within minutes, making stroke a medical emergency requiring immediate treatment.
facts: 40,000 stroke cases occur annually in Malaysia
Third leading cause of death globally
Leading cause of adult disability worldwide
Time-critical: “Time is brain” – every minute counts

types.ischemicDesc: Caused by a blockage (blood clot) that cuts off blood flow to part of the brain. Accounts for about 85% of all strokes.
types.ischemicNote: Most common type. Can be caused by blood clots formed in the brain (thrombotic) or clots that travel from elsewhere (embolic).
types.hemorrhagicDesc: Caused by bleeding in or around the brain when a blood vessel bursts. Less common but often more severe.
types.hemorrhagicNote: Can be intracerebral (bleeding within brain tissue) or subarachnoid (bleeding around the brain).

symptoms.title: Stroke Symptoms - Act F.A.S.T.
symptoms.subtitle: Recognizing stroke symptoms quickly and acting F.A.S.T. can save lives and reduce long-term disability.

fast.face2: Ask person to smile. Does one side droop?
fast.arms2: Ask person to raise both arms. Does one drift down?
fast.speech2: Ask person to repeat simple phrase. Is speech slurred?
fast.time2: If any signs present, call 999 immediately.

symptoms.emergencyAction: If you see any of these signs, call 999 immediately! Note the time symptoms first appeared – this information is crucial for treatment decisions.
otherList: Sudden dizziness or loss of balance

whatToDo.title: What to Do
list: Call 999 immediately. Don’t wait to see if symptoms improve
Note the time. When did symptoms first appear?
Stay calm and safe. Keep the person comfortable and safe

whatNotToDo.title: What NOT to Do
list: Don’t wait – Don’t wait to see if symptoms improve
Don’t drive – Don’t drive yourself or let the person drive
Don’t give medication – Don’t give aspirin or other medications

malaysianSpecific.title: Malaysian-Specific Risk Considerations
ethnic: Indians have higher stroke risk due to diabetes prevalence
Chinese populations show higher rates of hemorrhagic stroke
Malays have increased risk due to hypertension rates
lifestyle: Limited physical activity in urban areas
High stress from work and traffic congestion
Delayed medical attention due to cultural beliefs

prevention.title: Stroke Prevention
prevention.subtitle: Up to 80% of strokes can be prevented through lifestyle modifications and proper management of risk factors.
list: Quit smoking and avoid tobacco products
Manage stress and get adequate sleep

diet.title: Healthy Local Foods
cookingTips: Steam, grill, or bake instead of frying
Use herbs and spices for flavoring
Reduce oil and salt when cooking

management.title: Stroke Management
management.subtitle: Comprehensive stroke management involves acute treatment, rehabilitation, and long-term care to optimize recovery and prevent future strokes.
list: Lifestyle modifications and risk factor control

goldenHours.title: Acute Stroke Treatment - The Golden Hours
stages: 0–3 Hours: Optimal window for clot-busting drugs (tPA). Brain tissue can still be saved.
3–4.5 Hours: Extended window for tPA in selected patients. Still beneficial for many.
6–24 Hours: Mechanical thrombectomy may be possible for large vessel occlusions.
